messages:
alex: Quick sync re: routing policy plugin contract. I sketched a minimal interface that would let runtime and policy teams iterate independently. TL;DR: keep decide(ctx) -> ranked candidates + explain, and make hooks for caching and telemetry.

maria: can you paste the sketch? want to see shape, esp around fallbacks and region prefs.

alex: pasted below:

```
interface PolicyPlugin {
  decide(requestContext) -> List<{routeId, score, reasons[]}>
  onCacheHit(routeId, metadata)
  onObservation(requestContext, chosenRoute, latency, cost)
}
```

alex: Goals: tiny contract, no runtime blocking calls during decide (pure CPU + mem), allow async observations for telemetry, and make explainability deterministic.

sam: two quick concerns: 1) how do we handle incompatible model variants (quantized vs fp16) in the plugin? 2) what about multi-route hedging?

maria: for (1) I think the plugin should be passed a list of compatible route capabilities in ctx (so it can filter). For (2) we need a candidate flag (hedge_possible: true/false) and a hedging_budget param at runtime.

june: +1. Also want to call out performance: decide is invoked in the hot path for every request. The contract needs strict latency budgets (e.g., p99 < 0.25ms if implemented in native). If plugins are slower we should fallback to a built-in default policy.

alex: agreed. default fallback: simple cost*latency linear score with region_penalty. Plugins can opt-in to richer signals.

sam: about caching: if policy uses prefix/KV cache state, how should invalidation work? We can't let plugin state cause unsafe sticky routing.

maria: propose plugin-owned ephemeral keys only. Anything that affects cross-request affinity must go through runtime APIs: "policy.setAffinity(tenant, key, ttl)". That gives runtime control and visibility.

june: sounds good. Also need telemetry hooks so we can detect policy regressions: per-candidate latency histogram, miss rates, fallback rates. policy-bot can run sims nightly.

policy-bot: simulation run complete: delta against baseline policy -> 0.8% tail latency increase, -3.2% cost. Top cause: region_affinity decay window too long in 20% of traces.

alex: interesting — so we should add a decay_window parameter to the ctx signals (tenantAffinityAge) and let plugin tune. But default cap to 60s to avoid long-lived affinity leaks.

maria: operational concern: rollout. We need canary flags per-tenant + automatic rollback triggers (if tail latency regresses >2% or error rate +1%). Also require synthetic traffic probes exercising cold-cache and hot-cache scenarios.

sam: plus a staged rollout: simulate -> shadow -> 1% real traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> full. At each stage we run the eval harness comparing embeddings/outputs and routing economics.

june: interface addition: plugin should return optional "healthSignals" object (as flat list of strings) that runtime uses for auto-disable (e.g., "backpressure", "slow-db", "invalid-scores"). Keep it small: flags only.

alex: note: healthSignals must be best-effort and cheap to compute. We should never allow them to block decide.

maria: last thing: compatibility shim for older plugins — runtime will accept v1 (decide only) and v2 (decide+observe+health). v1 gets wrapped with default observe/health to keep telemetry consistent.

sam: docs action item: draft plugin contract + example in TS and Rust, include perf budget guidance and sample simulation harness. I'll take TS example.

june: ops action: add rollout checklist and gating in console; ensure canary toggles, probe traffic, and auto-rollback hooks exist.

alex: I'll update the RFC with interface sketch + example and add a note about caching/invalidation rules. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
thread_text: Quick sync re: routing policy plugin contract and rollout
